title: Terokkar Forest
body: Terokkar Forest spreads across the heart of Outland, a wood of olemba trees between the marshes of Zangarmarsh and the ash of Shadowmoon Valley. It is thought to take its name from Terokk, the mightiest king the arakkoa remember, and his bird-folk still keep their veils in its groves while his city of Skettis waits in the mountains to the southeast. The draenei once held this land. Tuurem was among the first of their cities to fall to the orcs, and their great necropolis of Auchindoun stands in the south. Two years ago a summoning by the Shadow Council tore Auchindoun open, and the blast scoured the forest around it into the Bone Wastes, where the restless dead now wander. Shattrath City rises in the northwest under the Sha'tar. The Alliance holds the Allerian Stronghold and the Horde holds Stonebreaker Hold, and both contend with arakkoa raiders, fel orcs, the blood elves of Firewing Point and the cultists of the Shadow Council.

title: Cenarion Thicket
body: In the forest's north, the Cenarion Thicket was a quiet outpost of the Cenarion Expedition, gathered around a tall tower among the trees. It is a place of the dead now. Something struck it in a blinding white light, and nearly every druid there died at once. Earthbinder Tavgren, away surveying the Bone Wastes at the time, came back to find only one other survivor: Warden Treelos, who still wanders the tower in shifting shapes, babbling of light and silence and of the eyes of Naphthal'ar atop the tower, which will not stop staring. The thicket's teromoths survived as well, but something has changed them: once at peace, they are agitated now and quick to attack.

parts.body: Samples taken from the vicious teromoths told Tavgren something new. They are infused with what feels like pure mana, the residue of a strong field of energy left behind by whatever struck the thicket. That energy did not kill the moths; it drove them into their agitated state instead.

title: Tuurem
body: Tuurem was a draenei town in the northern reaches of the forest, home to Vindicator Idaar before it became one of the first of his people's cities overrun by the orcs. Its ruins have not been left in peace. Broken of the Wrekt and other scavengers pick through the rubble, and there are rumors of artifact hunters robbing it of relics. Some of its old vessels still brim with raw magical energy, which the high elf Ros'eleth of the Allerian Stronghold hopes will help her scattered people resist the lure of demonic magic.

parts.body: Lately the town has served darker ends. Boxes of strange and exotic engineering parts, sold by an ethereal trader in Shattrath to the Broken merchant Empoor, were delivered here, and the last of them was found as a blood elf made ready to carry it on to Firewing Point.

title: Veil Reskk and Veil Shienor
body: Veil Reskk and Veil Shienor are arakkoa colonies in the northern woods, home to Shienor talonites, sorcerers and wing guards. Like every veil of the forest they answer to Skettis. Their warriors ambush hunters and couriers on the roads, strike at the garrisons by night, and escape through summoning circles before a warband can catch them. Each colony guards an Eye of Skettis, an orb enchanted by black art through which Terokk is said to watch over his colonies, and redeemed arakkoa in Shattrath long to look through them. The leaders of the two veils, Ashkaz of Reskk and Ayit of Shienor, are marked for death by the Alliance and the Horde alike.

title: Veil Skith
body: Veil Skith hides in a secluded grove just south of Shattrath, a colony of Skithian windrippers and dreadhawks led by Urdak. The Skithians are bold thieves who made off with a great shipment of exotic goods belonging to the ethereal Wind Trader Lathrai, and they carried children from a refugee caravan back to their cages here. Their altar, the Darkstone of Terokk, was raised for the colony's worship of Skettis, and those who would redeem the Skithians hold that it must first be purified.

parts.body: Kirrik the Awakened sent a rod blessed by the naaru A'dal to purify the Darkstone. When it was used, the altar exploded instead, and Kirrik, who felt the blast in his heart rather than heard it, judged that if the touch of A'dal could not bring the Skithians to redemption, nothing would: those who will not turn to the Light cannot be saved.

title: Stonebreaker Hold
body: Stonebreaker Hold is the Horde's town in the middle of the forest, an orc hold of watchtowers commanded by Rokag. Its people are a mixed lot. The blood elf Advisor Faila wonders what misstep earned her this posting, the troll Tooki warns that the forest holds worse juju than the Alliance, and Kurgatok bickers with his ill-mannered imp. Mawg Grimshot, who lost an eye to the bonelasher king, posts bounties on the beasts, and the trader Rakoria presses olemba seeds into oil to sell along the roads. Messengers run the dangerous road north to Swamprat Post in Zangarmarsh. For Malukaz the hold is something more: a return to a land his people once called home.

title: Allerian Stronghold
body: The Allerian Stronghold is the Alliance's foothold in eastern Terokkar. It bears the name of Alleria Windrunner, and many of its defenders are high elves who stayed in Outland: rangers walk its walls, and the seamstress Ros'eleth admits she once hoped to meet the town's namesake. Captain Auric Sunchaser commands, while Lieutenant Gravelhammer brings him one crisis after another, a burning sentry tower, a missing merchant, mercenaries from Honor Hold stirring up trouble. Trouble rings the garrison on every side. Arakkoa raid its roads, fel orcs dig in at the ruins to the east, and to the south lie the Bone Wastes, where at least one of its defenders flatly refuses to go, whatever the bounty.

title: Firewing Point
body: Firewing Point is a blood elf citadel in the northeast of the forest, its spire rising over a walled courtyard. Its masters serve Kael'thas, and through him Illidan, and its defenders, warlocks and bloodwarders guard some great work under way in that courtyard. The overseer Sharth Voldoun keeps to the top of the highest spire. A Cenarion envoy, Isla Starmane, came here on a diplomatic mission and found herself locked in a cage. On the river's banks to the south and southwest, the Alliance keeps the Allerian Post and the Horde keeps Stonebreaker Camp, small forward posts watching the spire.

parts.body: What the courtyard holds is a mana bomb, the second the blood elves have built. The forward posts have learned that its final code is held by Sharth Voldoun himself, overseer of the project, and that with that code the bomb could be set off right where it stands, in the heart of Firewing Point.

title: Bonechewer Ruins
body: East of the Allerian Stronghold lie the Bonechewer Ruins, where fel orcs of the Bonechewer have lately moved in and set to rebuilding. The work never stops: warped peons repair the buildings and raise fortifications day and night, while devastators and backbreakers stand guard and messengers watch the roads. Their arrival troubled both garrisons, for the Horde at Thrallmar had believed the fel orcs safely contained around Hellfire Citadel, and no one can yet say what has brought them so far from it.

parts.body: The answer lay in plans found in the camp, written in a hand far too delicate and precise for any orc. The Bonechewer take their orders from the blood elves of Firewing Point, and they were sent here to keep the garrisons occupied, though the plans do not say why.

title: Grangol'var Village
body: Grangol'var Village is a ruined settlement west of Stonebreaker Hold, on the northern fringe of the Bone Wastes. A shadowy band has moved into its broken buildings: robed summoners and executioners, initiates, laborers and advisors, all answering to one Shadowmaster Grieve. Who they are, no one outside the village yet knows, only that they are hostile. Scouts from both garrisons keep watch on the village entrances, though their reports went unanswered for more than a week.

parts.body: Their own gossip betrays them. A laborer grumbles that the Shadow Council is not paying him by the hour, and an advisor threatens to have strangers beaten. They are the Shadow Council, and Grieve leads the council in this village, offering any who cross him a grave in the labyrinth of Auchindoun or a place as a sacrifice to Murmur. Yet his cultists whisper among themselves that the council has lost all control of Murmur in the Shadow Labyrinth.

title: Bleeding Hollow Ruins
body: On the western border with Nagrand lie the Bleeding Hollow Ruins, until lately a village of Bleeding Hollow orcs. Boulderfist ogres fell on it in a cowardly night attack, and the survivor Jorin Deadeye fled to Garadar to beg for help. The ogres hold the village still. Their fat leader, Unkor the Ruthless, makes his lesser followers dance for him while he waits for something none of them will name, and Kilrath, a scout sent from Garadar, hides at the edge of the ruins, watching. To the Mag'har it is also one of the old villages of their ancestors.

title: Refugee Caravan
body: On the road south of Shattrath, at the northern edge of the Bone Wastes, a caravan of refugees from the Lower City sits stalled beside its wagons. Broken and humans, orcs and redeemed arakkoa traveled together until Shadow Council cultists struck in the night, and now their guards wait for the help called from Shattrath. Each traveler has a reason to be here. Kirrik the Awakened seeks his people in the colonies; High Priest Orglum came to cleanse the troubled spirits of the wastes; Soolaveen would ease the pain of the restless dead; Lakotae would heal the blasted land. A boy named Ethan simply wants his friends back, carried off by the bird men in the night.

title: The Bone Wastes
body: The Bone Wastes are a scar of dust and bleached bone at the heart of the forest, left where the blast from Auchindoun blew the land around the necropolis bare. The dead do not rest here. Lost spirits and broken skeletons, draenei corrupted by the explosion, wander in blind torment, and the bones of the fallen lie scattered for any who would carry them to a proper grave. Plague-carrying bonelashers, scorpids and burrowing bone worms prowl the sand, wood mites gnaw at the trees along its edges, and ethereal plunderers and Shadow Council cabalists pick over its tombs. Five spirit towers stand in the wastes.

parts.body: By ancient custom the living come to pay their respects at the spirit towers, though only at certain hours of the day. The spirits of Auchindoun have no stake in the quarrels of the living, but those who honor the towers in those hours hope to win their favor, and with it a boon.

title: The Shadow Tomb and the Tomb of Lights
body: Two tombs lie near the refugee caravan, and neither rests easy. The Shadow Tomb, to the west, has been taken over by Shadow Council cabalists, who guard its halls closely. To the east, buried under charred sand, lies the Tomb of Lights, a lost resting place of the dead. Ethereals plunder its bodies for keepsakes laid beside them centuries ago, and the Shadow Council has corrupted it so deeply that its draenei dead have risen as vengeful spirits, angry and confused, with a burning hatred for the living.

parts.body: Orders taken from the cabal explain the Shadow Tomb. Part of the Shadow Council is fleeing Auchindoun, and these cabalists use the tomb to store the powerful artifacts they carried out of the necropolis, among them the sacred relics of the patriarchs Arunen, K'alen and Atalor.

title: Veil Rhaze
body: Veil Rhaze was a particularly wicked colony of Skettis on the western edge of the Bone Wastes, west of the Shadow Tomb. The blast that tore Auchindoun apart destroyed it, but did not end it: the malevolent spirits of its people still haunt the ruins as deathtalons, screeching spirits and spirit ravens, bound to Terokk's will. Overhead circles Torgos, king of the bonelashers, who took Mawg Grimshot's eye while he hunted here. Torgos keeps away from an old arakkoan scarecrow called Torgos's Bane, and hunters say only the carcass of his mate Trachela, laid at its foot, will draw him down. She nests with the other bonelashers at Carrion Hill in the north of the wastes.

title: Veil Lithic
body: Veil Lithic lies in the southwest of the forest, a colony of Lithic oracles and talonguards loyal to Skettis. Its sorcerers practice an especially cruel art. They wrap unhatched eggs in a shadowy curse, so that the hatchlings which emerge are born as mindless servants of Terokk. Kirrik the Awakened of the refugee caravan asks those who would help to break the cursed eggs early, redeeming the hatchlings that can still be saved and putting down the ones the curse has already claimed. Even Kirrik admits it is grim work to meddle with another's hatchlings, but he holds that leaving the evil to brew would be bleaker still.

title: Auchindoun and the Ring of Observance
body: Auchindoun was the great necropolis of the draenei, born from a first tomb where Prophet Velen laid the remains of a fallen naaru, and the Auchenai death priests tended its dead for some five hundred years. Two years ago a Shadow Council summoning tore it open. Its four wings now hold rival powers: ethereals plunder the Mana-Tombs, the maddened Auchenai keep the Crypts, the Sethekk arakkoa hold their halls, and the Shadow Council struggles to contain Murmur, the being it called, in the Shadow Labyrinth. At its center lies the Ring of Observance, where draenei spirits drift among the stones, Lower City agents hold the door of the labyrinth, and the outcast death priest Ramdor grumbles over the bones.

title: The Shadow Stair
body: The Shadow Stair climbs to Auchindoun's northern entrance and the sealed doors of the Mana-Tombs, inside which the ethereal Nexus-Prince Shaffar plunders the crypt for all it is worth. Outside, a rival Consortium camp waits under Nexus-Prince Haramad, who greets visitors by asking those sent to kill him to take a number and wait their turn. His Captain Kaftiz swears that Shaffar's wards will break any minute now, while his artificers look for another way in and a shady dealer sells only to friends of the Consortium. They share the stair uneasily with Shadow Council cabalists, whose skirmishers and spell-weavers gather on its steps.

title: Sha'tari Base Camp
body: Southwest of Auchindoun, the Sha'tar have pitched a base camp in the wastes, where great elekk stand among Commander Ra'vaj's vindicators. Their war is with the Auchenai, and the battle on the Auchenai Grounds east of the camp has raged for days, every fallen soldier on either side snatched away and its soul lifted for some dark rite. The camp is beset on other fronts too: spiders from Netherweb Ridge raided it by night and carried off its people, and Oakun broods over a way to destroy the cursed thing that flies over the wastes. An Explorers' League dig under the hapless Chief Archaeologist Letoll shares the camp, hunting bone worms with a drum unearthed at their dig.

body: Northeast of Auchindoun, beyond its walls, rises the Writhing Mound, a place where necromancers gather. Auchenai death-speakers and doomsayers work their rites there among rats, broken skeletons and the restless bones of the dead, and the doom skulls they carry are laced with powerful necromantic enchantments. Pale death-spirits linger about the mound, and at its heart, ringed by the dead, lies a summoning circle.

title: Netherweb Ridge
body: On the southeastern edge of the Bone Wastes rises Netherweb Ridge, the lair of the dreadfang widows. The spiders hunt by night, poisoning their victims, wrapping them in webs and carrying them off to the ridge, where cocooned prisoners hang among the rocks. They struck the Sha'tari Base Camp this way, and the warriors who chased them into the dark did not return; Vindicator Haylen and his last companions lie poisoned just west of the ridge. Deep within lurks the brood-mother of them all, the great Terokkarantula, and while she lives the widows will keep on spawning.

title: Veil Shalas
body: At the foot of the cliffs beneath Skettis lies Veil Shalas, the most formidable of Terokk's colonies, home to Shalassi oracles and talonguards. Through Shalas the forward sages of Skettis wage their war on the Light, and four magical signal fires, burning emerald, violet, bloodstone and sapphire, carry word between the colony and its master. Kirrik the Awakened of the refugee caravan counts it the colony that must be silenced before anyone can begin to plot the fall of Skettis itself.

parts.body: One of the redeemed paid dearly for coming here. Skywing traveled to Veil Shalas to sway the Shalassi toward the Light, and they answered with the curse of Luanga the Imprisoner, one of Terokk's most feared agents, which left him a small fluttering bird. A stranger followed him back here, Luanga fell, and Skywing, free at last, declared that his mission now lay in Skettis.

title: Blackwind Landing
body: Blackwind Landing is the camp of the Sha'tari Skyguard in the northern Skethyl Mountains, just outside Skettis, where nether rays rest between sorties. The Skyguard is Shattrath's air wing, and after a sharp rise in arakkoa activity was followed by attacks on the city, it posted riders here to watch Skettis from above. The war is hard on them. Dozens of sorties fly each day, feed for the rays runs short, and scouts are knocked from the sky by monstrous kaliri. Sky Commander Adaris lies wounded in camp under the care of Severin, while Sky Sergeant Doryn drills new recruits. Nearby, in a cage, sits an arakkoa prisoner named Hazzik, cursing his captors.

title: Skettis
body: High in the Skethyl Mountains of southeastern Terokkar lies Skettis, the hidden city of the arakkoa, its dwellings rising around the waters of Blackwind Lake. From here Terokk's power reaches every veil in the forest. Its quarters of Veil Harr'ik, Veil Ala'rak and Upper and Lower Veil Shil'ak are guarded by wing guards, windwalkers and soulcallers, and by the strange time-lost arakkoa. Monstrous kaliri, bred as war birds, nest atop the dwellings. On the island of Terokk's Rest at the heart of the city, an old and nearly blind scribe named Sahaak keeps his books, and there, the talonpriests believe, their ancient king will one day return.

title: Earthbinder Tavgren
body: Earthbinder Tavgren of the Cenarion Expedition was away on a survey of the Bone Wastes when death came to the Cenarion Thicket. He returned to find his fellow druids slain and only Warden Treelos alive, his mind broken. Refusing to leave, Tavgren camped outside the thicket and set about learning what had happened, studying its agitated teromoths and a dead Broken found inside with a strange object beside him. A harmful aura still lingers about the place, he warns, the residue of whatever destroyed his friends.

parts.body: The trail of a merchant's boxes led from Tuurem to Firewing Point, and when the truth came back to him, it was a blood elf bomb of pure mana, a weapon able to take out whole towns. Tavgren could only ask why anyone would turn such a thing on a place of peace and repose, and hope that the reason, locked inside the head of Warden Treelos, might surface as his mind heals in time.

title: Captain Auric Sunchaser
body: Captain Auric Sunchaser is the high elf who commands the Allerian Stronghold and the high elves who chose to stay there. His days are a parade of bad news delivered by his aide, Lieutenant Gravelhammer: a fire in the sentry tower, a missing merchant, a Cenarion druid held captive at Firewing Point. He meets each report with weary questions about what else could possibly go wrong, yet every one ends with an order to see it handled, to call in the scouts or to notify anyone who can help.

parts.body: The captive was the Cenarion envoy Isla Starmane, and when she escaped Firewing Point it was to Sunchaser that she brought her full account of what the blood elves were doing there, distraught over the fate of the Cenarion Thicket. He thanked her rescuers on behalf of the whole stronghold, which he declared in their debt.

title: Rokag
body: Rokag commands Stonebreaker Hold, and he has little patience for anything that is not defense or supply. When Malukaz chatters about the forest's history, Rokag grants that the work matters but points out that someone must see to the defenses and logistics while the present's problems remain unsettled. His answer to the arakkoa is blunt: kill their leaders in Reskk, Shienor and Skith, and when he hears that some arakkoa in Shattrath claim friendship with the Horde, send a messenger to demand their surrender. He keeps the shadowstalker Kaide watching the fel orcs in the ruins to the east.

parts.body: Kaide's suspicions proved right. Plans taken from the fel orc camp showed the fel orcs colluding with the blood elves and ordered to keep the hold busy, something Rokag admitted he would never have guessed. He called it disturbing news, all the more because the plans did not say why.

title: Theloria Shadecloak
body: Theloria Shadecloak is a high elf who watches from the Allerian Post, a small watch north of the Bonechewer Ruins. She is an exile. When the Dark Portal opened she learned what had become of her people, and seeing the Farstriders throw in their lot with Kael'thas ended the homecoming she had dreamed of; her exile spared her their downfall, she says, but this forest is now the only home she has left. She keeps her eyes on the fel orcs in the ruins and means to stall any reinforcements they try to bring.

parts.body: Her watching turned up more than fel orcs. Over several days Theloria saw a blood elf woman come and go from the fel orc camp, plainly giving orders to its leader, and she let curiosity overrule her judgment far enough to shadow the woman north to the edge of Firewing Point.

title: Kirrik the Awakened
body: Kirrik the Awakened is an arakkoa who saw through Terokk. Where others in Skettis took him for a prophet, Kirrik named him a charlatan whose only true prophecy was the doom he brought about himself, and it was Kirrik who bravely led the exiles out of Skettis on their pilgrimage to Shattrath, where they learned of the Light through A'dal. Kirrik did not stay behind the city's walls. He went back out into the colonies in search of others who might be saved, and he now waits with the refugee caravan in the Bone Wastes, guiding strangers against the veils.

parts.body: The Darkstone of Veil Skith hardened his heart. When the altar exploded rather than yield to a rod blessed by A'dal, Kirrik concluded that if the touch of the naaru could not redeem his people, nothing would: those who have not given themselves over to the Light are mere servants of evil, and they must be destroyed.

title: Ramdor the Mad
body: Ramdor the Mad stands on the bone pile outside the Auchenai Crypts, scowling at spirits only he and a child can see. He was once a death priest of the Auchenai, a title he now finds unsavory. When Exarch Maladaar turned the priory to experiments in necromancy, Ramdor held that the dead they had cared for some five hundred years should simply be left alone, and he was cast out for his beliefs. He calls the Auchenai insane to the last, and those who only smile and nod at the boy's ghosts lambs and lemmings, yet the dead will not leave him in peace. Gruff as he is, he sees that the bones of the ancestors are properly buried.

parts.body: He is also, by his own admission, a liar. The treasure he promised for the book of the dead never existed; he lied to get the book and had no idea where the lost souls kept any treasure. Yet once it was in his hands he rewarded its bearer all the same, and welcomed them to the fold of those who see the dead.

title: Isfar
body: Isfar is an arakkoa who once followed the Sethekk. When Auchindoun exploded, the Sethekk took it as an omen of their master's arrival and marched out of Skettis with great fanfare to face their god in the temple ruins, and Isfar went with them, for his older brother Syth was one of their leaders. In time he came to doubt Syth and his ally Ikiss, and Syth had him cast out of the halls while keeping their sister Lakka prisoner. Isfar found safety in Shattrath but could not stay. He has crept back to the entrance of the Sethekk Halls, hoping to free Lakka and to restore the stolen relics of Terokk to his people.

title: Sky Commander Adaris
body: Sky Commander Adaris leads the Sha'tari Skyguard at Blackwind Landing, and he leads it from his sickbed. Badly wounded in a Skettis incursion, he drifts in and out of consciousness, muttering that unseen arakkoa are all around, watching and waiting. His healer Severin takes it for fevered delirium, the more so when Adaris demands an elixir of arakkoa shadow dust to see into a world of shadows where, he insists, the true leaders of Skettis dwell. Even from his bed the commander is stubborn, and slow to trust strange plans.

parts.body: The commander was right. The elixir opened a world of shadows, and in it dwelt the three talonpriests at the head of Skettis, clerics the Skyguard had heard of but never seen with their own eyes. Now Adaris knew why, and he sent his helpers to hunt them in Veil Ala'rak.

parts.body: His caution had a reason. Adaris feared a mutiny among his weary riders had he openly backed a plan to bring Terokk into the world, so he turned a blind eye to dealings with his arakkoa prisoner. Once persuaded, he committed his men fully, promising they would fly in support when the time came.

title: David Wayne
body: David Wayne is a human blacksmith who lives alone at Wayne's Refuge, a scrap of land just east of Firewing Point. He came to Draenor with the Sons of Lothar, and though he left Honor Hold behind, he says the Sons never quite leave a man. He cannot fully explain why he went. He only feels that he is not meant to be at Honor Hold right now, and that he may be meant to be part of something larger. For now he works his anvil and forge alone.

title: Teribus the Cursed
body: Teribus the Cursed is a winged creature of evil that flies over the Bone Wastes, a shadow high above the dust and bleached bone around Auchindoun. Nothing on the ground can reach it while it keeps to the skies, and it does not come down of its own accord. Those who would face it must first find some way to call it down to them.

parts.body: Oakun of the Sha'tar has a plan, a terrible one by his own account. Long ago a caravan went to Auchindoun to take a Dread Relic from the ancient tombs beneath the necropolis. They fled with it, but the relic was their undoing, for it summons evil when touched, and their wagons still lie wrecked to the east. That relic is the key to bringing Teribus down.

parts.body: The relic was brought back from the wreck, far more powerful than Oakun had feared. Carried to the summoning circle of the Writhing Mound and joined with enough doom skulls taken from the Auchenai necromancers there, it can command Teribus to come down and face whoever called it.

parts.body: The cursed thing could not refuse the summons. Called down to the circle at the heart of the Writhing Mound, Teribus came to fight whoever had called it, and there it was slain, and a great evil was purged from the skies over Terokkar.

title: Terokk
body: Terokk is the ancient king of the arakkoa, the mightiest their people remember, and the forest itself is thought to take its name from him. Skettis, the hidden city high in the Skethyl Mountains, was his seat, and every veil of the forest still answers to it. At the heart of the city lies the island that bears his name, Terokk's Rest, and there, its talonpriests believe, their king will one day return to the world.

parts.body: In the old tales Terokk was a hero. Arakkoa hatchlings are still told of his deeds and his splendid plumage, and of how he dwelt among his people for hundreds of years and then vanished, leaving behind only his mask, his spear and his writings. Those cherished relics are gone from Skettis now, borne away by the Sethekk when they left the city.
sources: quest 10098 description (hero; hatchlings told of his deeds and beautiful plumage; hundreds of years; vanished; mask, spear, writings; borne away by the Sethekk)

parts.body: Not all arakkoa revere him. The redeemed exiles of Shattrath, whom Kirrik the Awakened led out of Skettis, hold that Terokk was no prophet but a charlatan, and that the only doom he ever foresaw was the one he brought about himself.
sources: quest 10849 description (Kirrik recognized Terokk as a charlatan, not a prophet; the only prophecy was the doom of his own bidding; Kirrik led us from Skettis)

parts.body: The talonpriests mean to have him back. An almanac taken from one of them presages the return of the most terrible king in arakkoa history, and with each day, Rilak the Redeemed warns, Terokk comes closer to his full strength. Rilak, who long took such tales for legend, now holds that the only chance is to bring him into the world before he is ready.
sources: quest 11028 description (almanac presages the return of Terokk, most powerful and terrible Skettis king; mere legend; closer to full strength; bring him prematurely)

parts.body: His rule had a darker side. Hazzik, an arakkoa of the lowest caste held captive by the Skyguard, says that under Terokk he would have been sacrificed to the dark powers the talonpriests worshipped, and he would see their hopes for Terokk's return come to nothing.
sources: quest 11056 description (lowest caste; would have been sacrificed to the dark powers worshipped by his talonpriests; prevent them from succeeding)

parts.body: Called back to Terokk's Rest before his time, Terokk raged that the stars were not yet aligned and his powers failed him, and swore that whoever had called him would pay. He boasted that he could not be killed, that he was immortal. He was not. With Skyguard riders bombing from above, he fell.

title: The Mana Bomb
body: When word stopped coming from the Cenarion Thicket, the Cenarion Refuge, Stonebreaker Hold and the Allerian Stronghold each sent someone to look. They found Earthbinder Tavgren alone outside a thicket of the dead, his fellow druids slain by something swift and unnatural and only the mad Warden Treelos left alive. Tavgren means to get to the bottom of it. The thicket's teromoths have turned vicious and must be compared with their gentler kin, and inside, beside the body of a dead Broken, lies a strange object no one can explain. Whatever killed the druids, Tavgren is sure, left its traces behind.

parts.body: The vicious teromoths proved to be soaked in pure mana, the by-product of whatever struck the thicket. The Broken merchant Empoor, who travels the road between Tuurem and Shattrath, talked only once he had been beaten to within an inch of his life, and then admitted no more than that he carried boxes for an ethereal in Shattrath.

parts.body: Wind Trader Lathrai of the Lower City remembered nothing until his stolen goods were won back from the Skithian arakkoa of Veil Skith. Then his memory improved: about a month before, he had sold Empoor several boxes of strange and exotic engineering parts, and they had been delivered to Tuurem.

parts.body: A last box, found at Tuurem as a blood elf made ready to carry it to Firewing Point, held bomb parts, just as the garrisons had feared. The trail led on to the forward posts on the river below Firewing Point, where grim business waited.

parts.body: The garrisons struck at Firewing Point. Atop its highest spire Sharth Voldoun told an image of his master that the smaller prototype tested on the Cenarion Thicket had been a complete success, and that a second bomb was being fueled in the courtyard below. When the attackers came for him, the image bade him deal with them and then destroy their town. Instead they took his final code and set the bomb off in Firewing's own courtyard. With the overseer dead and the bomb destroyed, both garrisons celebrated their deliverance.

title: The Fel Orcs of the Bonechewer Ruins
body: Fel orcs have come to the ruins east of the garrisons and are building day and night. For the Alliance, Bertelm sends volunteers against their peons and on to Theloria Shadecloak at the Allerian Post; for the Horde, Kurgatok sends them against the same peons and on to Shadowstalker Kaide, watching from the trees. Thrallmar had believed the fel orcs safely contained around Hellfire Citadel, and harrying their workers will not be enough to stop them. Both watchers have made a discovery that may explain why the fel orcs are here.

parts.body: Both had seen the same thing: a blood elf woman coming and going from the fel orc camp, conferring with its leader and plainly giving orders. Each had shadowed her north to the edge of Firewing Point before turning back. Whose orders she carried, neither could say, but she was not to leave the camp again.
sources: quest 10002, 10003 descriptions (blood elf woman issuing orders; shadowed to Firewing Point; kill her before she leaves)

parts.body: The liaison, Lisaile Fireweaver, was hunted down before she could leave the camp. That bought a little time, the watchers judged: the blood elves would grow curious about what had become of their friend, and by then the garrisons hoped to understand what they intended.
sources: quest 10002, 10003 objectives and reward texts (Lisaile Fireweaver slain; bought a little time; curious about their friend)

parts.body: Plans found in the camp, written in a hand far too delicate and precise for any orc, gave part of the answer. The Bonechewer were there to serve the blood elves, and they had been ordered to keep the garrisons occupied. Why, the plans did not say.
sources: quest 10012, 10013 descriptions and reward texts

parts.body: The Alliance could not strip its garrison for an attack, so Theloria's volunteers thinned the ranks of the Bonechewer devastators and backbreakers themselves while she looked for ways to stall reinforcements. Things began to look up: if the fel orcs could be kept from reinforcing, she judged, the post could be held.

parts.body: Kaide, for his part, wanted the fel orcs bloodied badly enough that their presence would never draw notice beyond Stonebreaker. If word reached Thrallmar that the fel orcs had not been contained, the hold would receive a great deal of unwanted company. Some stories, he told his helpers, are best left where they happened.

title: The Shadow Council at Grangol'var
body: A shadowy band has moved into the ruins of Grangol'var Village, and the scouts who spotted it, Private Weeks for the Alliance and Scout Neftis for the Horde, waited more than a week for anyone to answer their reports. When help finally arrives, each scout knows only that the newcomers are hostile. Each has a flimsy disguise ready for anyone willing to slip into the village and listen to three of its more talkative residents, an initiate, a laborer and an advisor, though a few hunters among them may see through it, and leaving the village will undo it.

parts.body: Between them the truth came out. The initiate complained that the interruption meant starting his work over, the laborer grumbled that the Shadow Council was not paying him by the hour, and the haughty advisor threatened to have the stranger beaten. These were the Shadow Council, led here by Shadowmaster Grieve, who promised his enemies burial in the labyrinth of Auchindoun or sacrifice to Murmur. The scouts were aghast.

parts.body: Back went the intruders, weapons drawn, to cut down executioners and summoners and Grieve himself. Lieutenant Gravelhammer and Advisor Faila agreed that a Shadow Council stronghold on their doorstep was the last thing either garrison needed, and rewarded those who had prevented it.

title: The Wolf Spirit
body: Malukaz of Stonebreaker Hold came to Terokkar through Nagrand, and found to his joy that not all of his people's old ways were lost. Generations ago, he says, when orc clans still called this forest home, the wolf spirit had a place in their lives. When the orcs departed they left it behind, and in time it grew lonely and left the forest too. Malukaz means to call it home. For his ritual vestments he needs the pelts of the forest's timber worgs, and for the final piece the pelt of Ironjaw, the old and cunning patriarch of the wolves who roams the northeast.

parts.body: With incense made in the days of the clans burning by the runestone in his hut, Malukaz called to the spirit: his people had given themselves to evil and forgotten it, but now they had returned to honor it again. The wolf spirit answered, and Malukaz declared that Thrall would be proud. Perhaps, he mused, the spirit had been waiting all along for the orcs to see what their choices had wrought.

title: The Eyes of Skettis
body: Weary of arakkoa raids, Rokag of Stonebreaker Hold sends a messenger to Shattrath to demand the surrender of Rilak the Redeemed, leader of the arakkoa there. Lady Dena Kennedy of the Allerian Stronghold sends hers to learn their secrets instead, and Kirrik the Awakened sends on the travelers he meets in the wastes. Rilak has a task for all of them. Terokk, he says, watches his colonies from Skettis through orbs enchanted by black art, and Rilak wants the Eyes of Skettis stolen from Veil Reskk and Veil Shienor, so that he may see what Terokk sees.

parts.body: To the Horde's demand Rilak gave no surrender, only an explanation. The Horde's people were angry, he granted, but there was little he could do: some arakkoa had been touched by the power of the naaru and were forever changed, while those who remained in the wild were as they had always been.
sources: quest 10862 reward text

parts.body: The Alliance envoy, sent only to learn, found Rilak glad of the visit. He called the Allerian Stronghold wise to seek him out, and promised that there was much he could show of his people and their secrets.
sources: quest 10863 description (learn the secrets of their race) and reward text (you are wise to find me; much that I can show you)

parts.body: The Eyes showed Rilak that Terokk's gaze was fixed on the south. He sent a missive telling what they had seen to Kirrik the Awakened, who had once named Terokk a charlatan and led the exiles out of Skettis, and who now waited with the refugee caravan in the Bone Wastes.

parts.body: Kirrik began a campaign against Terokk's colonies, and its first test went awry. The Darkstone of Veil Skith, touched with a rod blessed by A'dal, exploded rather than be purified, and Kirrik judged that arakkoa who would not turn to the Light must be destroyed.

parts.body: The blows that followed fell hard. The vengeful spirits of Veil Rhaze were put down, the cursed eggs of Veil Lithic broken before the curse could seep in, and the signal fires of Veil Shalas put out. Kirrik knew such blows could not go unanswered, and sent word to Rilak that Terokk would surely seek revenge.

Shattrath was safe for now, Rilak said, but dark skies still loomed over Skettis, and only tomorrow knew what Terokk would send next.

title: The Book of the Dead
body: Outside the Auchenai Crypts a draenei child, Ha'lei, sees the dead all around him. Nobody believes him, not even his mother, except the outcast death priest Ramdor, who sees them too and grows angry about it. Ramdor holds that the dead the Auchenai cared for so long should be left alone, while Exarch Maladaar has turned to necromancy. Wanting the spirits to leave him in peace, Ramdor promises treasure to anyone who will bring him the book of the dead, held, he says, by the Aldor Ezekiel of Shattrath.

parts.body: Ezekiel at first claimed never to have heard of the book. Then he admitted that he had lied: the book had been stolen, probably by refugees, and since Auchindoun was defunct he had no more use for it anyway. He had seen ruffians snooping around the terrace, now likely dicing in the slums of the Lower City.

parts.body: The ruffians, once cornered, confessed they had sold the book to a pair of draenei for a great deal of gold. The younger of the two kept talking of his master's grand design, and they said they lived at the old Abandoned Armory north of Telaar, in Nagrand.

parts.body: There Nitrin the Learned grieved for his son. He had turned a blind eye to the signs: Levixus had been communing with demons, who offered him power and then gave him a taste of it, and now the boy had the book. His plans were known only to his father and his dark master, and he had to be stopped.
sources: quest 10251 reward text

parts.body: Levixus stood atop the ruins of Auchindoun, reading from the book, calling the dead by name and binding their tortured souls to his will. To fight what cannot be seen, Nitrin brewed a tincture, and only then admitted that it was the initiation rite of Auchindoun's death priests: whoever drinks it sees the world of the dead forever.
sources: quest 10252 description and reward text

parts.body: Levixus fell, and the book went to Ramdor rather than being destroyed as Nitrin had asked. Ramdor confessed that he had lied to get it and had never known of any treasure. Still he rewarded his visitor, and pointing to the spirits now visible all around, he welcomed them to the fold.

title: Refugees of the Bone Wastes
body: The refugee caravan out of the Lower City has stopped in the northern Bone Wastes after Shadow Council cultists fell on it, and scouts have gone to Shattrath for help. Its guards believe the danger has passed. The Broken refugee Mekeda does not, and asks for the cultists gathered at Auchindoun's northern entrance to be driven off before they return to slit throats in the dark. All Broken were once draenei, Mekeda says, and the spirits of the ancestors dwell in Auchindoun.

parts.body: Orders taken from the cabal were written in a simple shadow cypher, which Mekeda had learned living among the outcasts of the Lower City. They revealed that part of the Shadow Council was fleeing Auchindoun and hiding powerful artifacts in the Shadow Tomb to the west, among them the relics of three patriarchs, Arunen, K'alen and Atalor.

title: The Fallen Exarch
body: In the Bone Wastes the vindicators of the Sha'tar under Commander Ra'vaj have battled the Auchenai for days on the grounds east of their camp, with no end in sight. Worse than the losses is what follows them. Every body that falls, Auchenai or Sha'tar, is snatched from the field and its soul lifted away. Ra'vaj will not let the fiends feed their rituals on his dead. With proper burial out of the question, he hands out torches to burn every corpse on the field, though he fears it will not be enough.

parts.body: It was not enough, and a hero was needed. Strikes on the Auchenai initiates and doomsayers kept them busy while his scouts slipped behind their lines, and what the scouts found was worse still: the Auchenai had dragged a coffin out of the Auchenai Crypts and were feeding it stolen souls. The scouts believed it held the first exarch of the crypts, whom the Auchenai meant to raise.

parts.body: Fighting through to the western side of Auchindoun, following the walking souls, a hero destroyed the coffin's contents before the stolen souls could revive them. Ra'vaj declared the victory theirs, and reckoned the defeat would set the Auchenai back by several weeks.

title: The Skyguard over Skettis
body: The Sha'tari Skyguard welcomes recruits who can fly, but first it wants to see whether they can fight. Those who prove themselves in Shattrath are sent on with a package of explosives to Sky Sergeant Doryn at Blackwind Landing, the camp outside Skettis. There the work begins at once. The arakkoa are breeding monstrous kaliri to use against the Skyguard's scouts, and recruits must blast the hatcheries atop the city's dwellings while dodging the great birds that guard them. Scouts shot down over the city must be led out on foot, and the hungry nether rays taken to the woods to hunt warp chasers. All the while the wounded Sky Commander Adaris raves that the true masters of Skettis are hidden from sight.

parts.body: His healer Severin humored him with an elixir brewed from arakkoa shadow dust, and it proved him right. It revealed a world of shadows where the three talonpriests of Skettis, Ishaal, Skizzik and Zellek, had hidden all along, clerics the Skyguard had heard of but never seen. They were said to dwell in Veil Ala'rak, near Blackwind Lake.

title: The Return of Terokk
body: One of the slain talonpriests, Ishaal, carried a mysterious almanac full of arcane symbols and charts of celestial bodies, written in what seems an ancient form of the arakkoa tongue. Sky Commander Adaris, his vision blurred by loss of blood, could not read it. Before drifting back into unconsciousness he sent it to the one arakkoa he trusts, Rilak the Redeemed of the Lower City. In the camp at Blackwind Landing, meanwhile, the Skyguard keep a caged arakkoa prisoner, Hazzik, who curses his captors and swears his cage will not hold him for long.

parts.body: Rilak read in the almanac the coming return of Terokk, the most terrible king in arakkoa history. He had always believed it legend. Now, with the talonpriests at work, he saw only one chance: to bring Terokk into the world before he regained his full strength, and he sent the news back to Adaris.
sources: quest 11028 description

parts.body: Adaris would not hear of it. Hurrying Terokk's return was madness to him, and the matter now purely military. But Hazzik, born to the lowest caste that Terokk's talonpriests once sacrificed, quietly offered a bargain behind the commander's back: the talonpriests must not succeed, whatever Adaris said, and Hazzik had something useful hidden at his old dwelling in Upper Veil Shil'ak.
sources: quest 11028 reward text (out of his mind; purely military matter)
quest 11056 description

parts.body: It was a disguise, one of the shabby ones Hazzik used to make for ethereal smugglers of rare books. In it a stranger fooled Sahaak, the old and nearly blind scribe of Terokk's Rest, into handing over the Adversarial Bloodlines, a catalogue of the descendants of Terokk's ancient enemies. Prophecy held that their deaths would be followed by Terokk's return.
sources: quest 11029 description and reward text

parts.body: The descendants, held captive by the talonpriests, were Gezzarak the Huntress, the crystal giant Karrog, the heretic Darkscreecher Akkarai and Vakkiz the Windrager. Called forth at the summoning circles of Skettis, each was slain, and from tokens of the fallen Hazzik made an offering that could summon Terokk himself.
sources: quest 11885 description and reward text

parts.body: At last Adaris relented. He had turned a blind eye to the dealings with his prisoner, fearing a mutiny if he backed them openly, and now he sent his riders. Called to Terokk's Rest before the stars aligned, Terokk fell, and Adaris swore the Skyguard would be forever in the debt of those who brought him down.
